deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The surrounding pages solve the family of septic trinomials x^7 - 3x^2 + A = 0 for a sequence of complex constants A. These are labelled 'Gleichung', grouped into 'Parallele', with one 'Zugabe'. On this page Gauss finishes the 'dritte Gleichung' (A = 2 - 2i) and works the 'Gleichung Vier' (A = (2 - sqrt2) - sqrt2 i). Logarithms are 7-place base-10 with characteristic 10 suppressed. A trailing 'n' marks a negative number.

METHOD (made explicit by me, and verified against every number on the page).
- Write A = c e^{iC} and x = r e^{i phi}.
- The equation says the three vectors x^7, -3x^2 and A sum to zero. Multiply by e^{-2i phi} and by e^{-7i phi} and take imaginary parts. This gives r^7 sin(5 phi) = c sin(2 phi - C) and 3 r^2 sin(5 phi) = c sin(7 phi - C). This is the law of sines in the triangle of the three terms.
- Write s2 = sin(2 phi - C), s5 = sin(5 phi), s7 = sin(7 phi - C). Eliminating r gives the single equation in phi:
  7 log|s7| - 2 log|s2| - 5 log|s5| = log(1/lambda), with 1/lambda = 3^7 / c^5 and log 3^7 = 3.3398488.
- Then r^7 = c s2/s5, so log r = (log(s2/s5) + log c)/7. Finally x = r(cos phi + i sin phi).
- If s2/s5 < 0 the actual argument is phi + 180 deg (s2 is unchanged, while s5 and s7 change sign).
- Each trial phi is refined by one step of regula falsi / Newton in 7th-decimal units per arc-second. The tabulated per-second differences of log sin are multiplied by k*k for k = 2, 5, 7 (power times chain factor). For example 2*2*(-195.5) = -782, 5*5*(-292.2) = -7305, 7*7*(-116.2) = -5693.8.

(1) TOP: third equation, A = 2 - 2i, so log c = 0.4515450, C = 315 deg, log(1/lambda) = 1.0821238.
- Trial phi = 153 deg 40'7". Angles: 2phi - C = 352 deg 20'14", 5phi = 48 deg 20'35", 7phi - C = 40 deg 40'49". log|sin| values: 9.1249682, 9.8734007, 9.8141393.
- 2*9.1249682 = 8.2499364; 5*9.8734007 = 9.3670035; their sum is 7.6169399; 7*9.8141393 = 8.6989751. Difference: 1.0820352.
- Defect 886 divided by the derivative 1359 gives 0.652", so phi = 153 deg 40'7.652".
- log(s2/s5) = 9.2515675, with derivative -406.5 per second, times 0.652 gives -265, so 9.2515410. Adding log c gives log r^7 = 9.7030860, hence log r = 9.9575837 (r = 0.90695).
- s2/s5 < 0, so the true argument is phi + 180 deg. Root: x = +0.8128500 - 0.4022866 i.
- The block 153.40.8 / 352.20.16 / 48.20.40 / 40.40.56 just recomputes the angles for 153 deg 40'8".

(2) Second root of the same equation.
- Trial 163 deg 58'53". Angles: 12 deg 57'46", 99 deg 54'25", 112 deg 52'11". The log sums give 1.0820031, defect 1207, derivative -709.6, so phi is about 51.30".
- Recomputed at 163 deg 58'51". Angles: 12 deg 57'42", 99 deg 54'15", 112 deg 51'57". The logs give 1.0821453. Gauss writes the correction as +205 and gets phi = 163 deg 58'51.289".
- log(s2/s5) = 9.3573486, plus 58, gives 9.3573544. Adding log c gives 9.8088994, so log r = 9.9726999. log|cos| = 9.9828002 (negative), log sin = 9.4408423.
- Root: x = -0.9026100 + 0.2591446 i.

(3) 'Gleichung Vier': A = 0.5857864376 - 1.4142135624 i = (2 - sqrt2) - sqrt2 i.
- log sqrt2 = 0.1505150 (negative imaginary part); log 0.5857864 = 9.7677393; tan C = sqrt2/(2 - sqrt2) = tan 67.5 deg, and log sin 67.5 deg = 9.9656153.
- So C = 292 deg 30', log c = 0.1505150 - 9.9656153 = 0.1848997, log c^5 = 0.9244985, log(1/lambda) = 3.3398488 - 0.9244985 = 2.4153503.

(3a) Root near phi = 143 deg 10'32".
- Angles: 353 deg 51'4", 355 deg 52'40", 349 deg 43'44". The logs give 2.4153134, defect 369, derivative 2393.2, so phi = 143 deg 10'32.154".
- log(s2/s5) = 0.1732060 with derivative 2(-195.5) - 5(-292.2) = 1070, corrected by +165. Adding log c gives 0.3581222, so log r = 0.0511603.
- Root: x = -0.9005516 + 0.6742972 i.

(3b) Root near phi = 145 deg 59'38".
- Angles: 359 deg 29'16", 9 deg 58'10", 9 deg 27'26". log|sin| values: 7.9513300 (negative), 9.2383547, 9.2156671. The logs give 2.4152362, defect 1141, derivative 12598.6, so phi = 145 deg 59'38.090".
- log(s2/s5) = 8.7129753 with derivative -5299, corrected by -480, gives 8.7129273. Adding log c gives 8.8978270, so log r = 9.8425467 (r = 0.6959).
- Gauss's cos/sin logs 9.9159620 n and 9.7531951, and his result +0.5724674 - 0.3942227 i, are struck out, with the note 'S. unten'.
- My reconstruction: since s2/s5 < 0, the argument is 325 deg 59'38" and the root is about 0.5769 - 0.3891 i.

(3c) Root near phi = 146 deg 48'36".
- Angles: 1 deg 7'12", 14 deg 3'0", 15 deg 10'12". The logs give 2.4163409, derivative -2605.7, so phi is about 39.8".
- Recomputed at 146 deg 48'40". Angles: 1 deg 7'20", 14 deg 3'20", 15 deg 10'40". The logs give 2.4152996, defect 507, so phi = 146 deg 48'39.805".
- log(s2/s5) = 8.9065678 with derivative 1730, corrected by -337, gives 8.9065341. Adding log c gives 9.0914338, so log r = 9.8702048.
- Root: x = -0.6206730 + 0.4059860 i.

(3d) Root near phi = 3 deg 52'29".
- Angles: 75 deg 14'58", 19 deg 22'25", 94 deg 37'23". The logs give 2.4152989, defect 514, derivative -1600.7, so phi = 3 deg 52'28.679".
- log(s2/s5) = 0.4646656, corrected by +92, gives 0.4646748. Adding log c gives 0.6495745, so log r = 0.0927964.
- Root: x = 1.2353858 + 0.0836707 i.

Purpose: tabulating all seven roots of x^7 - 3x^2 + A as A moves along lines ('Parallele') in the complex plane. This is evidently a worked example of how the roots move with the constant term, of the kind relevant to the topology of the fundamental theorem of algebra and to Gauss's treatment of trinomial equations.
errors: In the refined computation of the second root of the third equation, 1.0821238 - 1.0821453 = -215 units, but Gauss writes 205. The correction should be 215/709.6 = 0.303", giving phi = 163 deg 58'51.303" rather than 51.289". The first iteration had already predicted about 51.30". The effect on the root is negligible, of order 1e-7.

In root (3b), at about 145 deg 59'38", the logs of cos and sin used (9.9159620 n, 9.7531951) are wrong for this angle. The correct values are log cos 34 deg 0'22" = 9.91856 and log sin = 9.74769. The resulting value +0.5724674 - 0.3942227 i is therefore inaccurate. Gauss himself struck it out and referred elsewhere ('S. unten'). The correct root, with the argument shifted by 180 deg because s2/s5 < 0, is about 0.5769 - 0.3891 i.
All other logarithm multiplications, sums, differences, derivative combinations, interpolation steps and final roots check correctly to the precision used.

results.what: Numerical solution of complex roots of the trinomial x^7 - 3x^2 + A = 0 via the polar/triangle (law-of-sines) reduction. The equation becomes a single real equation in the argument phi, s7^7/(s2^2 s5^5) = 3^7/|A|^5, with modulus r^7 = |A| s2/s5. It is solved by logarithms and linear interpolation per arc-second.
results.modern_name: Trigonometric/logarithmic method for complex roots of trinomial equations (polar decomposition, Newton/regula falsi refinement)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, 'Beiträge zur Theorie der algebraischen Gleichungen' (1849, treatment of trinomial equations); related work by Euler/Lagrange on solution of equations by approximation

results.modern_name: Root tracking / root locus of a polynomial family as the constant term varies
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (root-path ideas around the fundamental theorem of algebra); systematic root-locus methods are 20th century (Evans 1948, in a different context)

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful routine logarithmic computation by a known method for trinomial equations, which Gauss himself published on. The only point of interest is the systematic tracking of roots along lines of the parameter, plausibly tied to his fundamental-theorem-of-algebra or trinomial work. That fits his known interests.

'ru = log r' is likely 'r̄u' or simply a label meaning log r; the value 9.9575837 is log r.
The '-1207' under the 163 deg 58'53" block and '+205' are Gauss's interpolation defects; the second should mathematically be 215.
The isolated 'r.... 9.8702048' line belongs to the 146 deg 48'39.805" root (log r), not to the struck-out 145 deg 59' column.
